column1: # The verb surface of the dispatch scheme.
# THIS FILE IS THE EXPECTATION. It is transcribed from the dispatch's own
# table and from the two ratified concept documents, and it is deliberately
# NOT derived from the built code: a probe that reads its expectation out of
# the thing it is probing checks that two copies agree, never that either is
# right. Both expositions are probed against this one file and neither is the
#   class     carried | uncarried | refusal | binding | extension
#   verb      the platform verb name, or '-' where the row names no verb
#   path      the form, exactly as it must appear
# THE OUTWARD FORMS -- carried, uncarried, refusal
# What a caller writes. These are probed END TO END against a running service
# and a running database: each is called and must be answered by the surface
# rather than by the framework's own not-found. That is the coverage half.
# `carried` rows are the thirteen verbs of the dispatch. `uncarried` rows are
# the four verbs the scheme does not carry, each of which must answer a typed
# category error naming the reason -- never a 404, never an unimplemented
# path, never a silent absence. The `refusal` row is a writing verb on a
# What the framework may have registered. These are probed STATICALLY against
# the annotations, and that is the closure half: a route outside this list is
# There are fewer bindings than outward forms, and the reason is measured
# rather than chosen. Quarkus REST 3.33.2, measured 2026-09-01: a path
# template takes the whole segment it appears in, and a narrowing regex on it
# is ignored -- so `@Path("{id}:send")` registers as `{id}` and the eleven
# colon verbs would collapse into one route. The colon is therefore split off
# in the surface, from a table the probe reads separately. The outward form is
# unchanged; only where the split happens moved.
# REST is extensible while an extension adds no effect: reads, projections,
# protocol furniture. State changes come from a verb, without exception. Every
# extension is DECLARED, which is what lets the probe check closure at all.
